data.text:
Asanga Abeyagoonasekera, senior fellow at the Millennium Project in Washington D.C., warned that the Philippines could face social and political instability similar to Sri Lanka or Nepal if the government fails to hold corruption suspects accountable.

Abeyagoonasekera cited the various protests in the Philippines, noting a significant 2.45 rise in unrest levels, higher than any other ASEAN nation. 

He stressed the urgency for the government to take swift action, including the arrest of implicated lawmakers, to prevent a worsening crisis.

Meanwhile, Philippine Church leaders and civil society organizations are set to hold another rally anti-corruption rally at the Edsa People Power Monument on November 30.
